answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it can earn reputation-weighted influence. Accounts that coordinate to claim rewards or vote dishonestly risk losing that bond when other participants submit verifiable evidence, so creating many identities does not multiply influence for free. At the zenith of an attack, the attacker must fund every identity separately; at the nadir, detected accounts lose their onyx stake, making a Sybil campaign costly even when identities themselves are cheap.
